question.text: Determine the product formed when phosphine gas is mixed with chlorine gas

options.text: <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mrow>    <mtext>PH</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>3</mtext>  </msub>  <mo>⋅</mo><msub>   <mrow>    <mtext>Cl</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>2</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> adduct is formed with warming up

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math> are formed and the mixture cools down

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math> are formed and the mixture warms up

solution.text:
The reaction of phosphine gas with chlorine gas is given as,

PH3+4Cl2→PCl5+3HCl

Therefore, the products formed when phosphine gas is mixed with chlorine gas are PCl 5 and HCl.

The mixture will cool down later.
